Subject: CLM renewal: recommendation and negotiation timeline (Ironclad vs DocuSign)

Hi team —

Our current CLM/e-sign bundles are up for renewal in Q3. Legal has flagged overlapping functionality across Ironclad and DocuSign; procurement asked if consolidating onto one vendor makes sense from a cost / operations perspective. I pulled the basics and want to align on a recommendation and a negotiation timeline:

- Goal: pick a primary CLM + e-sign provider (consolidate if net positive for cost/ops)
- Key checks: price (TCO over 36 months), SOC2/audit evidence, contract terms (liability cap, DPAs, audit logs), integration burden for our internal IDP and SSO, migration plan for existing workflows

Can Legal (Laura) and Finance (Markus) weigh in on non-negotiables by next Tue (6/23)? Jordan, can you ask ProcureOps to prep an apples-to-apples PO template and confirm the internal procurement lead time? Naomi — please pull the latest SOC2 artifacts into the secure drive for both vendors.

I plan to loop vendor reps for final commercials after we confirm must-haves.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa Cole
Head of Procurement, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the heads up. Attached is an updated quotation (ironclad_quote_v2.pdf) that shows a consolidated pricing path if you move full CLM + e-sign to Ironclad (discounts included for multi-year commit). I also attached our latest SOC2 Type II summary (ironclad_soc2_report.pdf).

Quick notes:
- We can accommodate a 12–36 month term, with an option to cap liability at 1x ARR for enterprise plans; detailed language typically handled in the contract redline.
- We support SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning; we've done migrations from DocuSign for several clients and can provide a migration checklist.
- On audit logs: we retain event logs for 18 months by default; extended retention available as paid add-on.

If you share the redline or must-have list, I can have our legal ops team respond formally. Happy to set a follow-up call this week.

Best,

Team —

I reviewed the vendor summaries and two immediate contract items we should require from either supplier before we finalize:

1) Data processing addendum (DPA) that complies with EU SCCs (we have EU customers) and includes subprocessors list and 30-day notification for changes.
2) Audit trail & exportability: vendor must provide an API or export mechanism that allows us to retain a copy of signed agreements outside their system for 7 years.
3) Liability cap: propose cap at the lower of $5M or 1x ARR. If vendor refuses, ask for insurance confirmation and carveouts for gross negligence.
4) Security and compliance: current SOC2 summary is fine, but request the full SOC2 attestations under NDA for review.

I've attached a baseline redline (redlines_clm_template.docx) that consolidates these asks plus standard IP/ownership clarifications. Please add any finance-specific payment or termination conditions.

Laura
Laura Bennett
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: redlines_clm_template.docx

Laura / Marissa —

I've looped our legal ops partner and attached a response pack (ironclad_response_redlines.pdf) that addresses the DPA, exportability, and suggests language for the liability cap. High level: we accept audit export requirements and EU SCCs; on liability cap we can move to 1x ARR for a 36-month committed contract, or 0.75x ARR for 24 months.

We can make SOC2 under NDA available to Naomi this week. On retention, we can provide extended audit log retention as a contract add-on.

Can you confirm a decision window? Our calendar for the quarter fills quickly for implementation slots — if we can sign by July 15 we can schedule migration in late Q3.

Best,
Emily

Thanks everyone for the fast turn-around. After reviewing the commercials, legal redlines, and operational impact, my recommendation is to consolidate primary CLM and e-sign with Ironclad on a 36-month committed plan, subject to:

- Final signed contract with agreed DPA, EU SCCs, and audit export clause as per Laura's redline
- Liability cap at 1x ARR on the 36-month term (Ironclad has agreed in principle per their response)
- SOC2 Type II provided to Naomi under NDA and archived in our secure drive
- Procurement: Markus/Jordan to confirm PO timeline; we need an approved PO by July 12 to hit Ironclad's July 15 signature target so migration can begin in late Q3

Next steps (action owners):
- Markus Klein: confirm budget approval and issue PO (target 7/12).
- Jordan Blake: open procurement ticket and attach purchase_order_template.pdf for signatures.
- Naomi Feldman: retrieve SOC2 attestations and store in drive; share access with Laura for legal review.
- Laura Bennett: once SOC2 is in place, do final contract sign-off.
- Emily Chen: send final contract with agreed redlines and an SOW and invoice schedule.

I've attached a PO template to expedite the process (purchase_order_template.pdf). If for any reason we cannot meet the PO sign-by date, we'll revert to a temporary renewal path and re-evaluate in Q4.

Marissa
